title: Felix and the Machine
premise: Astrid Nystrom, a disgraced navigator hauling cargo through contested orbits, discovers the nine-second gravity flicker was a signal from the cryosleep backups in her own hold—thousands of minds, including her own original body, uploaded by a fallen government before its collapse. The ruling Consortium wants the backups destroyed to cement its claim as humanity's only legitimate continuation; a resistance faction wants them woken all at once, which would crash the system's life support. Astrid must choose which half of humanity wakes, and in doing so confronts the copy of herself who remembers why she fled. She ends the stalemate by waking neither half whole: she releases the backups into a distributed network of ships, scattering them beyond any power's reach, and surrenders her own seat at the navigator's console to the version of herself that stayed behind.
about_author: J. M. Almeida is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade relaying messages between ships that rarely saw each other. They write about people who keep systems running and are never thanked for it.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Mid-haul through contested orbits, gravity fails across the system for exactly nine seconds; cargo drifts, crew panic, then everything snaps back as if nothing happened. Astrid alone notices the flicker matched a checksum pattern she hasn't seen since the war. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine competence.

chapters.title: The Hold That Sleeps
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She inspects the sealed hold she's been paid never to open and finds the cryo racks humming out of rhythm—counting down. Flashbacks establish the fifteen years of staying invisible and the debt that forced her to take this contract. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing like a body rising in water.

chapters.title: Manifest of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Tomas, her engineer, POV. Tomas decrypts the hold's manifest: forty thousand backup minds, flagged 'sovereign property, do not wake.' He confronts Astrid, who admits she knew—or suspected—and took the job anyway because the money would clear her name. Emotional beat: betrayal between friends who both need the money.

chapters.title: The Consortium's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Consortium auditor Vey POV. A polite boarding party arrives with questions about the nine seconds; Vey is charming, thorough, and clearly knows what's in the hold. Astrid performs ignorance while Vey plants a tracker. Emotional beat: the horror of being seen after years of successful hiding.

chapters.title: What the Original Remembered
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, intercut with a backup's dream-logs. We learn Astrid is herself a copy—the original Nystrom stayed behind during the evacuation and was uploaded into the hold. The flicker was the backups calling their own navigator home. Emotional beat: vertigo of self-doubt; which memories are hers?

chapters.title: Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Three factions converge on Astrid's ship: Consortium enforcers, resistance cells claiming the backups as martyrs, and scavengers smelling salvage. A running firefight forces her to burn fuel she can't spare. Emotional beat: claustrophobic escalation; invisibility is over.

chapters.title: The Resistance's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Resistance leader Okafor POV. Okafor argues all forty thousand should wake at once—justice demands it—but the math shows the surge would brown out the station habitats for months. Astrid sees idealism and body count wearing the same face. Emotional beat: sympathy curdling into alarm.

chapters.title: Vey's Offer
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Vey returns, off the record: destroy the backups, and the Consortium will restore Astrid's original rank, name, and legal existence. It's everything she's wanted for fifteen years, gift-wrapped. Emotional beat: temptation rendered as kindness, which makes it worse.

chapters.title: Static Between Selves
chapters.summary: Backup-Astrid POV (dream-state). Inside the hold, the sleeping copy of Astrid begins waking enough to speak through the ship's comms. She doesn't beg; she asks questions Astrid can't answer about who abandoned whom. Emotional beat: uncanny intimacy, a mirror that talks back.

chapters.title: Fuel, Debt, and Other Currencies
chapters.summary: Tomas POV. With the ship damaged, Tomas trades secrets to a scavenger captain for fuel, accidentally confirming the hold's contents to the black market. Now everyone knows. Emotional beat: the sick click of a small compromise becoming a catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Vote Nobody Called
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter. Crew, resistance passengers, and even the waking backups debate what to do—wake all, wake none, wake some. Astrid refuses to decide and hates herself for it. Emotional beat: democracy as an alibi for cowardice.

chapters.title: Gravity Learns to Lie
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The flickers return, longer now, and Astrid realizes they aren't a signal—they're a weapon test. Someone is using the backup network's processing substrate to prototype gravitational control. The Consortium isn't afraid of the sleepers; it wants their hardware. Emotional beat: revelation reframing every prior fear.

chapters.title: Okafor's Martyrdom
chapters.summary: Okafor POV. Cornered by Consortium forces, Okafor attempts to force-wake the racks early, believing martyrdom will galvanize the resistance. Astrid stops her physically, and the two women fight in the freezing hold among the sleeping dead. Emotional beat: grief and fury; justice and suicide indistinguishable.

chapters.title: The Name I Sold
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid nearly accepts Vey's deal—signs the destruction order—then finds her original's final log: the original chose to stay behind so a copy could live free, not so the copy could buy back a cage. She burns the order. Emotional beat: quiet, costly refusal.

chapters.title: Blackout Cascade
chapters.summary: Tomas and Vey alternating POV. The Consortium moves to seize the ship by force; Tomas sabotages the docking clamps, and Vey, watching her clean operation become a bloodbath, hesitates for the first time. Emotional beat: loyalty under fire; an antagonist's first crack.

chapters.title: Conversation in Cryo-Light
chapters.summary: Both Astrids, finally face to face via the hold's interface. The original explains the flicker: the backups built a consensus protocol—a way to distribute themselves across thousands of ships so no one power could ever own or erase them again. They need one navigator to execute it. Emotional beat: reconciliation without absolution.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The choice crystallizes: wake the backups onto the network (scattering them forever, including her original, who will never be embodied again) or let the Consortium sterilize the hold. Time runs out as boarding torpedoes lock on. Emotional beat: the weight of an irreversible decision made in minutes.

chapters.title: The Scattering
chapters.summary: Climax, ensemble POV. Under fire, Astrid executes the distribution protocol; the backups stream outward on every open channel, riding stolen bandwidth into a thousand vessels. Gravity stabilizes as the weapon-test substrate dissolves. Vey stands down rather than fire on a ship full of refugees no longer aboard. Emotional beat: exhiliration braided with mourning.

chapters.title: What Vey Reports
chapters.summary: Vey POV. Writing her official report, Vey falsifies it—recording the hold as destroyed—to protect the scattered minds and, unknowingly, herself. Justice outside the law arrives through a bureaucrat's small treason. Emotional beat: redemption earned quietly, undeservedly, believably.

chapters.title: Two of Everything
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Aftermath aboard the battered ship: the original's voice remains in the nav system as a distributed presence, neither alive nor gone. Astrid grieves and keeps flying. Tomas stays; Okafor leaves to tell the resistance the truth, whatever it costs her. Emotional beat: bittersweet settling.

chapters.title: Cargo Run, Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, epilogue-in-motion. Months later, Astrid takes ordinary contracts, but now faint flickers of distributed minds ride along in her console, helping her thread dangerous space. Staying invisible is impossible; being unownable is enough. Emotional beat: hard-won peace, vigilance intact.

chapters.title: The Navigator Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Final chapter, dual POV converging. On the anniversary of the flicker, every ship in the system experiences nine seconds of perfect stillness—a greeting, not a warning. Astrid answers aloud, and somewhere in the network, her original answers back. Emotional beat: closure as connection; memory as a living thing.
